speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your episodes of unresponsiveness in detail: how long do they last, what triggers them, and do you witness any specific movements like eye blinking or lip smacking?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (evolving from generalized absence seizures).

Given the recurrent staring episodes lasting 3–4 minutes, post-ictal lethargy, and the specific description of "muddy taste" and "hand gestures" (which may be automatisms or post-ictal confusion rather than typical myoclonic jerks), this presentation is highly suspicious for a seizure disorder that has progressed to status. I need to confirm the seizure type and rule out other causes immediately.

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)
REQUEST IMAGES: None at this time, as EEG is the gold standard for this clinical picture.
